# relgap outdated

Scans the project at path (default: the current directory) the way 'relgap pins' does and
compares each pin with the newest stable version on the tool's release line.

CURRENT is the version a pin stands for. An exact pin is itself. A value marked ≈ allows
more than one version, and the notes say which one relgap used: a constraint (~&gt; 1.15) takes
the highest exact pin of the tool in the same repository that satisfies it, otherwise the
lowest version that does; a prefix (26, prefix:1.2) takes the highest stable version that
starts with it; the latest channel is the latest version. Other channels (lts) aren't
compared.

BEHIND, BREAKING and DEPRECATION come from the digest of CURRENT..LATEST, the same digest
'relgap digest &lt;tool&gt; &lt;current&gt;..' prints. Entries below --min-confidence aren't counted.

relgap finds the latest versions with GraphQL queries of 10 to 25 tools, sent in parallel.
Only pins that are behind, and constraint and prefix pins, need a tool's full release list;
constraint and prefix pins start loading it at the same time.

tfprovider and chart pins are looked up in the Terraform registry and Artifact Hub, which name
the repository. Pins of tools without a GitHub repository, and image and action pins, are
skipped; --format json lists them with the reason.

EOL shows whether CURRENT's release cycle has reached its end on endoflife.date (yes, no, or
? when endoflife.date doesn't list the cycle), for tools whose registry entry names a
product. --format json also has the state of LATEST's cycle. VULNS counts the OSV
vulnerabilities of CURRENT, and how many of them upgrading to LATEST fixes. Both sources
are cached for a day. When one is down, relgap warns and prints the rest.

--binaries also reads the Go build info of each pinned tool's installed executables (on
PATH and in mise's installs directory) and lists the OSV vulnerabilities of the Go version
and main module they were built with. Like govulncheck's binary mode, minus the check that
the binary calls the vulnerable code.

--format sarif writes a SARIF 2.1.0 log for GitHub code scanning, located at each pin's
file and line: a result per pin behind latest (outdated), per pin on an EOL cycle (eol), per
upgrade with breaking changes or deprecations (breaking, deprecation), per advisory that
affects a pin (one rule per OSV ID), and per pin or file that failed (failed). The results
don't depend on --fail-on.

--fail-on takes breaking, deprecation, eol, vuln and outdated. Each value counts findings:
outdated counts the pins further behind than --max-behind (major:N, minor:N, patch:N,
releases:N or days:N; empty means any pin behind latest), breaking and deprecation count
the pins whose digest has such an entry, eol counts the pins on an EOL cycle, and vuln
counts the advisories that affect a pin at or above --vuln-severity. A value whose count
reaches --min-count (default 1) exits 3. Otherwise a tool or file that failed exits 1, and
so does an endoflife.date outage under --fail-on eol or an OSV outage under --fail-on vuln,
since a pass on partial data proves nothing.

## Usage

```sh
relgap outdated [path] [flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | no | no |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--binaries` | also check the Go version and main module of the pinned tools' installed executables against OSV | bool |  |  |  |  |
| `--fail-on` | exit 3 when this matches: breaking, deprecation, eol, vuln or outdated; repeatable (config policy.fail\_on) | list, repeatable |  | `breaking`: a breaking change in the range<br>`deprecation`: a deprecation in the range<br>`eol`: a pinned version past its end of life<br>`vuln`: a known vulnerability in a pinned version<br>`outdated`: a pin further behind than --max-behind | [`policy.fail_on`](/reference/config#policy-fail-on) |  |
| `--max-behind` | how far behind --fail-on outdated allows, such as minor:2, releases:10 or days:90 (config policy.max\_behind) | string |  | `major:1`: at most one major version behind<br>`minor:2`: at most two minor versions behind<br>`patch:5`: at most five patch versions behind<br>`releases:10`: at most ten releases behind<br>`days:90`: the first newer release is at most 90 days old | [`policy.max_behind`](/reference/config#policy-max-behind) |  |
| `--md-max-chars` | cut Markdown output to this many characters at a row or section boundary; 0 means no limit | int | `60000` |  |  |  |
| `--min-count` | findings a --fail-on value needs before it exits 3 | int | `1` |  |  |  |
| `--out` | also write the report to a file as format=path (repeatable); format is one of plain, md, json, sarif or github | string, repeatable |  | `plain`: table without color<br>`md`: Markdown<br>`json`: JSON envelope for scripts<br>`sarif`: SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning<br>`github`: GitHub Actions annotations |  |  |
| `--vuln-severity` | lowest rating --fail-on vuln counts: low, medium, high or critical; empty counts all (config policy.vuln\_severity) | string |  | `low`: CVSS 0.1 to 3.9<br>`medium`: CVSS 4.0 to 6.9<br>`high`: CVSS 7.0 to 8.9<br>`critical`: CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 | [`policy.vuln_severity`](/reference/config#policy-vuln-severity) |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `md`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Fail-on values

`--fail-on` makes the command exit 3 when the report has a match:

| Value | Matches |
|---|---|
| `breaking` | a breaking change in the range |
| `deprecation` | a deprecation in the range |
| `eol` | a pinned version past its end of life |
| `vuln` | a known vulnerability in a pinned version |
| `outdated` | a pin further behind than --max-behind |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 3 | A --fail-on gate matched. The report is still written. |
| 4 | Credentials were missing or rejected for every source the command needed. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
relgap outdated
relgap outdated ~/src/infra --format md
relgap outdated --fail-on outdated --max-behind minor:2
relgap outdated --fail-on eol --fail-on vuln --vuln-severity high
relgap outdated --fail-on outdated --min-count 5 --format sarif > relgap.sarif
relgap outdated --binaries --format json | jq '.data.binaries[]'
relgap outdated --format json | jq '.data.pins[] | select(.status == "outdated")'
```
